chunks: And from him, from Al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Samaan, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "When the Mu'adhdhin establishes the Iqamah, speech becomes forbidden, unless the people do not have a known Imam."

key_terms.إِقَامَة: Iqamah (the second call to prayer, signaling the start of the prayer)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to speak during the Iqamah in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) delineates the transition from the Adhan to the Iqamah, establishing silence as a condition of reverence once the prayer commences, while providing a practical exception for communities lacking a recognized leader. In Shia jurisprudence, this highlights the importance of congregational order and the role of the Imam in maintaining the sanctity of the prayer ritual. The ruling underscores the shift from the preparatory phase of the Adhan to the active performance of the prayer during the Iqamah.
